text: Three are fruits. Which picture does not fit?
Look for the one that grows as a vegetable root.
a carrot is a root vegetable, not a fruit. Carrots grow as roots underground; apples, pears, and plums are fruits.
Three carry people from place to place. Which picture does not fit?
Which picture can carry a traveller?
a tulip is a flower, not a way to travel. A bus, train, and boat carry people; a tulip grows in a garden.
Three are clothes you can wear. Which picture does not fit?
Find the thing that belongs at the table.
a plate is used for food, not worn as clothing. A hat, sock, and coat are clothes; a plate holds food.
Three describe weather in the sky. Which picture does not fit?
Which picture could you pack for lunch?
a sandwich is food, not weather. Sunshine, rain, and snow describe weather; a sandwich is something to eat.
Three help people build or fix things. Which picture does not fit?
Look for the toy instead of a workshop tool.
a balloon is for play, not for making or fixing things. A hammer, saw, and spanner help people build or repair; a balloon is a toy.
Three animals live in the sea. Which animal does not fit?
Which animal needs a burrow rather than the ocean?
a rabbit lives on land, not in the sea. Dolphins, octopuses, and sea turtles live in the ocean; rabbits live on land.
Three shapes have four straight sides. Which shape has only three?
Count the straight sides, one at a time.
a triangle has three straight sides. A square, rectangle, and rhombus each have four straight sides; a triangle has three.
Three pictures are blue. Which picture is a different colour?
Check the colour, not what the object is.
the ball is red; the other three pictures are blue. A colour can be shared by different things: a bird, fish, and kite can all be blue.
Three pictures have wheels. Which picture has none?
Look underneath each thing for round wheels.
a kite has no wheels. A bicycle, car, and pushchair roll on wheels; a kite flies on a string.
Three animals have stripes. Which animal has spots instead?
Look for spots instead of long bands.
a ladybird has spots, not stripes. Tigers, zebras, and many bees have stripes; a ladybird has round spots.
Three pictures can be seen in the daytime sky. Which picture belongs on a person?
Look for the picture that belongs on a person.
a boot belongs on a foot, not in the sky. The sun, clouds, and rainbows can be seen in the sky; a boot is worn on a foot.
Three shapes have straight sides. Which one has only a curved edge?
Trace the outside edge with your finger.
a circle has no straight sides. A triangle, square, and rectangle have straight sides; a circle has only a curved edge.
Three cards show an even number of dots. Which card does not fit?
Touch each dot once, then try making pairs.
it has three dots, so one dot is left when you try to make pairs. An even number can be arranged into pairs with none left over.
Three words start with B. Which word starts with a different letter?
Look at the very first letter in each word.
cat starts with C; the other three words start with B. The first letter is the one at the left of a word.
Three shapes have more than three corners. Which shape has exactly three?
Tap each corner as you count.
a triangle has exactly three corners. A triangle has three sides and three corners. The other shapes have more.
The repeating set uses circles and squares. Which shape is outside that set?
Check whether each shape is a circle or a square.
a triangle is outside the circle-and-square set. A repeating set can use two shapes in a pattern. This one uses circles and squares.
Three pictures are large. Which picture is small?
Compare each picture with the others, not its name.
the small star is smaller than the other three pictures. Comparing size means looking at how much space each picture takes up.
Three numbers are even. Which number is odd?
Try making pairs. Which number has one left over?
five is odd; it cannot be split into two equal groups. Two, four, and six can be paired with none left over. Five leaves one extra.
What comes next? Look for the rule.
A pattern follows a rule. Look for a group of shapes that comes back in the same order.
Coral, blue; coral, blue. The two colours repeat in that order.
Look at the first two colours. Do they come back in the same order?
Gold, leaf; gold, leaf. The two shapes repeat in that order.
Watch which shape comes after the gold star.
Purple diamond, sun; purple diamond, sun.
Find the two-shape part that keeps coming back.
Leaf, coral; leaf, coral. The order stays the same.
Start at the first shape and follow the same two-step order.
Blue square, gold star; blue square, gold star.
What shape follows the blue square each time?
Sun, purple diamond; sun, purple diamond.
Look for the pair that repeats.
The coral group grows by one each time: one, two, three, then four.
Count the circles in each group. How many are added?
The star groups grow by one: two, three, four, then five.
Count each group and notice how much it grows.
Two leaves, then one drum. That three-shape group repeats.
Find the short group: two matching leaves, then a drum.
Two gold stars, then a blue square. Repeat that group.
Which shape comes after the two gold stars?
One purple diamond, then two drums. Repeat that group.
Look for one diamond followed by two drums.
Two suns, then one leaf. The three-part group repeats.
Notice the two suns together before the leaf.
Coral, blue, leaf; then coral, blue, leaf. Three shapes repeat.
Look for the three shapes that return in the same order.
Star, diamond, drum; then the same three shapes again.
The repeating part has three different shapes. Which comes first?
Square, leaf, sun; square, leaf, sun. The order repeats.
Follow the first three shapes, then follow them again.
Drum, circle, diamond; then drum, circle, diamond.
Which three-shape group starts with a drum?
Two coral circles, then a blue square. That group repeats.
Look for two matching circles before the square.
One leaf, then two blue squares. Repeat that group.
Find one leaf followed by a pair of squares.
Two purple diamonds, then a sun. Repeat the group.
Which shape ends the group of two purple diamonds?
One drum, then two gold stars. The group repeats.
Look for a drum followed by two matching stars.
Leaf, circle, square, sun; then the same four shapes.
This rule has four steps. Follow each one in order.
Square, diamond, sun, drum; then that four-shape group again.
Trace the four different shapes in order.
Each drum group has one more drum: one, two, three, then four.
Count the drums. Each new group adds one.
The leaf groups grow by one: two, three, four, then five.
Compare the group sizes. What is added each time?
